title: PokéBonk, Two Screens
tagline: The game up top. The things I press down below.
what: I made PokéBonk feel at home on the Thor, a two-screen handheld. The game stays up top; menus, touch controls and a keyboard move downstairs. It is Charcher’s browser game, with my Steam wrapper and two-screen add-on around it.
built: Wrapped the browser game in its own Steam-launched window
Moved menus and controls downstairs instead of showing the same page twice
Made one controller highlight travel between both screens
Added a touch keyboard and full-size choices on the bottom screen
progress: The two-screen rework shipped in October 2026.

remix.changed: I built the Linux Steam wrapper and two-screen add-on. PokéBonk itself is Charcher’s game.

making.problem: The browser game was made for one screen. I wanted the Thor’s other screen to have a job.
how: I launch the game in its own browser window from Steam, with my add-on loaded.
The add-on moves the game’s own controls below, leaving more room to read above.
The controller highlight crosses between screens; touch and a keyboard work below too.

broke.title: Look up, press down
broke.body: In the Pokédex, the Pokémon and its stats sit above while the collection and search sit below. I can pick the next one without covering what I am reading.

proof.caption: The real Pokédex across both screens, before the October layout rework.

credits: Steam wrapper and two-screen add-on: me
